questions.stem: A branch VPN address object is synchronized to two Fabric members, but both receive the same subnet. Which object-side control changes the allocation semantics?

options.text: Enable ipam-allocate-unique on the IPAM Fabric address object.
options.feedback: That flag requests a distinct IPAM subnet on each Fabric FortiGate instead of inheriting one shared subnet.

options.text: Create a second firewall policy referencing the same object.
options.feedback: A policy reference changes traffic matching, not IPAM allocation; the address object's subnet remains shared.

options.text: Set the address object to type fqdn and enable fabric-object.
options.feedback: FQDN objects resolve names to addresses and do not allocate subnets from IPAM pools.

options.text: Increase the DHCP lease duration on the branch interface.
options.feedback: DHCP lease duration does not control firewall-address object allocation or Fabric uniqueness.

questions.stem: An IPAM address object receives a subnet from the wrong pool. Which configuration relationship should be checked first?

options.text: The FortiGate policy's inspection mode.
options.feedback: Inspection mode is evaluated after address allocation and cannot select an IPAM pool.

options.text: The IPAM rule's Apply to Addresses setting and address-name match.
options.feedback: IPAM rules can select firewall addresses by name pattern; a missed or unintended match sends the object to a different allocation rule.

options.text: The VPN gateway's IKE version.
options.feedback: IKE version does not determine which IPAM rule allocates the address object.

options.text: The Fabric connector's heartbeat interval.
options.feedback: Heartbeat timing affects Fabric connectivity, not the address-name rule used by IPAM.

questions.stem: A VPN gateway should consume a centrally managed client range rather than a manually typed static range. Which design fits the FortiOS 8.0 feature?

options.text: Create a DHCP reservation for every remote user.
options.feedback: DHCP reservations are not the IPAM firewall-address range mechanism used by the VPN gateway.

options.text: Use an FQDN address object as the client pool.
options.feedback: An FQDN object represents name resolution, not a subnet pool for VPN client allocation.

options.text: Reference an IPAM-type firewall address as the VPN gateway address range.
options.feedback: FortiOS 8.0 allows IPAM firewall-address objects to supply automatically allocated ranges for VPN clients.

options.text: Enable a local-in policy on the VPN interface.
options.feedback: Local-in policy controls traffic to the FortiGate itself and does not allocate client addresses.

questions.stem: What proves that per-device unique IPAM allocation actually occurred?

options.text: The CSF connector status shows Connected.
options.feedback: Connected proves Fabric communication, not that each member received a different subnet.

options.text: The firewall address object has a non-empty comment.
options.feedback: A comment is metadata and provides no evidence of the allocated subnet.

options.text: The VPN gateway reports that IKE is established.
options.feedback: IKE establishment does not prove which subnet IPAM allocated to clients.

options.text: Compare the resulting subnet value of the same Fabric address object on each FortiGate.
options.feedback: A successful sync only proves distribution; the distinct allocated subnet values prove the per-device allocation result.

questions.stem: FortiManager's pxGrid connector has TLS connectivity to ISE but no connected users appear. Which ISE-side step is explicitly required?

options.text: Approve the pending FortiManager client in Cisco ISE pxGrid Services.
options.feedback: FortiManager must be approved as a certificate-based pxGrid client; transport connectivity alone does not authorize event import.

options.text: Disable certificate validation on the FortiManager connector.
options.feedback: Disabling validation weakens trust and does not perform the ISE client-approval step.

options.text: Create a new FortiGate static route for each endpoint.
options.feedback: Endpoint routes do not authorize FortiManager to consume pxGrid events.

options.text: Change the ADOM from Normal to Advanced mode.
options.feedback: ADOM mode is not a substitute for approving the pxGrid client in ISE.

questions.stem: ISE reports a session state of Authenticated, but FortiManager does not import that user. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: FortiManager only imports IPv6 users.
options.feedback: The pxGrid connector is not limited to IPv6 identities.

options.text: FortiManager processes Started, Postured, and Disconnected; Authenticated is ignored.
options.feedback: The connector filters session states; an ISE state outside the supported set can be ignored even when pxGrid is healthy.

options.text: The user must have a local FortiManager administrator account.
options.feedback: Connected-user import does not require each endpoint user to be a FortiManager administrator.

options.text: The endpoint must send DHCP Option 82 before ISE can publish it.
options.feedback: Option 82 is unrelated to pxGrid session-state filtering.

questions.stem: Where should an operator verify the new Device Type and Session State fields in FortiManager 8.0?

options.text: In the FortiGate routing monitor only.
options.feedback: Routing monitors do not display pxGrid endpoint classification fields.

options.text: In the FortiManager firmware upgrade history.
options.feedback: Upgrade history does not show imported connected-user attributes.

options.text: In the pxGrid Connected Users table or the pxGrid connector diagnostic output.
options.feedback: The 8.0 enhancement exposes these attributes in the GUI connected-user table and CLI output.

options.text: In the FortiAnalyzer report scheduler.
options.feedback: The report scheduler is unrelated to pxGrid connector user context.

questions.stem: A distributed ISE pxGrid payload references node FQDNs that FortiManager cannot resolve. What should be fixed?

options.text: Add those FQDNs as FortiGate firewall address objects.
options.feedback: Firewall address objects do not provide name resolution to the FortiManager connector.

options.text: Change the endpoint Device Type to Unknown.
options.feedback: Device Type does not fix DNS resolution for ISE nodes.

options.text: Disable the pxGrid session-state filter.
options.feedback: Session-state filtering does not resolve node names.

options.text: Configure DNS on FortiManager to resolve every ISE node FQDN used by pxGrid.
options.feedback: The connector requires DNS resolution for all ISE nodes because monitoring-node payloads can reference pxGrid node FQDNs.

questions.stem: An analyst changes the FortiAnalyzer Threat Posture Timeline from Traffic to Threat Score. Should the agent run again?

options.text: No; changing the metric toggles the chart without starting a new analysis.
options.feedback: The metric selector changes the plotted series; a timeframe change, not a metric toggle, triggers a new retrieval and analysis.

options.text: Yes; every widget toggle forces a new FortiAI retrieval.
options.feedback: The guide states that switching Traffic, Sessions, and Threat Score does not trigger new analysis.

options.text: Only if the endpoint has no alerts.
options.feedback: Alert presence does not change the documented metric-toggle behavior.

options.text: Only after exporting the PDF.
options.feedback: PDF export is an output action, not the trigger for reanalysis.

questions.stem: The analyst changes the selected timeline window from one day to seven days. What should be expected?

options.text: Only the x-axis labels change; the agent never re-fetches.
options.feedback: That describes a chart-only metric toggle, not a timeframe change.

options.text: FortiAI fetches related logs again and performs a new analysis for the new timeframe.
options.feedback: The selected timeframe is part of the agent's retrieval; changing it starts another data fetch and analysis.

options.text: The incident is automatically closed and reopened.
options.feedback: Timeframe selection does not automatically change incident state.

options.text: The endpoint is removed from Asset Identity Center.
options.feedback: Changing the analysis window does not delete or de-register the asset.

questions.stem: The Threat Posture Timeline menu is unavailable for an administrator. Which prerequisite should be checked?

options.text: The FortiSwitch DHCP server whitelist.
options.feedback: That is an unrelated switch security control.

options.text: The FortiGate IPAM subnet pool size.
options.feedback: IPAM capacity does not govern FortiAnalyzer FortiAI entitlement.

options.text: FortiAI licensing and the administrator's access rights.
options.feedback: The timeline requires a valid FortiAI license and an administrator with appropriate access.

options.text: The endpoint's 802.11mc responder role.
options.feedback: Wireless ranging does not grant access to FortiAI analysis.

questions.stem: A timeline shows a threat-score spike. Which evidence best supports the analyst's interpretation?

options.text: Rely only on the generated summary paragraph.
options.feedback: A summary is an interpretation layer and should be checked against the source evidence.

options.text: Assume every device in the Fabric sent logs because the chart rendered.
options.feedback: A rendered chart does not prove complete source-device logging.

options.text: Use the current time instead of the selected timeline range.
options.feedback: The analysis is bounded by the selected time window, so timestamps must be checked against it.

options.text: Inspect the related alerts and source logs for the selected window and correlate their timestamps.
options.feedback: The timeline exposes the underlying alerts and source logs; the AI summary is not proof that all telemetry was collected.

questions.stem: The SOC wants to preserve the analysis for case review. Which supported action is available from the timeline?

options.text: Export a PDF or create/add the analysis to an incident.
options.feedback: The More menu supports PDF export, creating a new incident, or adding the information to an existing incident.

options.text: Install the analysis as a FortiGate firewall policy.
options.feedback: The timeline is not a policy-installation interface.

options.text: Convert the endpoint into a DHCP server.
options.feedback: The timeline does not change endpoint network roles.

options.text: Rotate the FortiAnalyzer administrator password.
options.feedback: Password administration is outside the timeline action set.

questions.stem: A DHCP client receives an address but its ARP packets fail DAI. What state should be inspected first?

options.text: The FortiAnalyzer report retention period.
options.feedback: Log retention does not populate the FortiSwitch DAI binding database.

options.text: The FortiSwitch DHCP-snooping binding for that MAC, IP, VLAN, and interface.
options.feedback: DAI uses the snooping binding database; a client lease alone does not prove that the switch learned the expected binding.

options.text: The FortiGate IPsec phase-2 selector.
options.feedback: IPsec selectors do not determine local VLAN ARP validation.

options.text: The FortiManager ADOM revision number.
options.feedback: An ADOM revision does not validate the endpoint's ARP source binding.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly separates DHCP snooping, DAI, and IPv4 source guard?

options.text: DAI builds DHCP leases; snooping blocks ARP; source guard changes DNS.
options.feedback: Those roles are reversed and DNS is not the source-guard function.

options.text: Source guard creates VLANs; DAI performs DHCP relay; snooping assigns IP addresses.
options.feedback: These features do not replace VLAN creation, DHCP relay, or address allocation.

options.text: Snooping builds bindings; DAI validates ARP; source guard restricts source IPv4 traffic.
options.feedback: The binding database is the shared state source, while DAI and source guard enforce different packet checks.

options.text: All three features are independent and never share state.
options.feedback: DAI and source guard can consume the DHCP-snooping binding information.

questions.stem: An administrator changes DHCP snooping from monitor to enable. What database effect must be planned for?

options.text: Both databases are guaranteed to remain unchanged.
options.feedback: The client database is specifically deleted on monitor-to-enable.

options.text: Only the trusted DHCP server list is deleted.
options.feedback: The documented transition affects the client database, not just the server allow-list.

options.text: The switch automatically converts every dynamic entry to a static entry.
options.feedback: The mode transition does not convert dynamic bindings to static records.

options.text: The DHCP client database is deleted during that transition.
options.feedback: FortiSwitch documents that monitor-to-enable clears the client database, so enforcement may start before bindings repopulate.

questions.stem: A statically addressed printer must pass source guard but never obtains a DHCP lease. What is the correct design step?

options.text: Add a static DHCP-snooping binding for the printer's MAC/IP/VLAN/port.
options.feedback: Static entries provide the binding state needed for endpoints that do not learn their address through the observed DHCP exchange.

options.text: Mark every access port as trusted.
options.feedback: Trusting all ports defeats the trust boundary and does not create the required endpoint binding.

options.text: Disable all DHCP snooping on the VLAN.
options.feedback: Disabling snooping removes the binding source rather than adding a valid static entry.

options.text: Create a FortiAnalyzer event handler for the printer.
options.feedback: An event handler does not populate the switch's binding database.

questions.stem: A FAP443K in an outdoor US deployment has no usable 6 GHz channel. Which constraint is most important?

options.text: The FAP443K must use 2.4 GHz as its AFC control channel.
options.feedback: AFC channel grants concern 6 GHz operation, not a 2.4 GHz control channel.

options.text: The FAP443K is SP-only and needs GPS/AFC channel authorization.
options.feedback: The Community troubleshooting tip distinguishes the FAP443K from the FAP441K: the 443K cannot use the LPI fallback and requires AFC/GPS.

options.text: The FortiGate must enable DHCP Option 82 on the SSID.
options.feedback: Option 82 is unrelated to 6 GHz regulatory channel authorization.

options.text: The AP must be placed in a FortiNAC Access Point Management group.
options.feedback: That is a wired NAC feature, not an AFC prerequisite.

questions.stem: The controller country code is set to Canada, but the APs are physically in the United States. Why can channels be missing?

options.text: The AP automatically converts every Canadian channel into an FCC channel.
options.feedback: The AP does not ignore the configured regulatory domain.

options.text: The SSID uses WPA3 instead of WPA2.
options.feedback: Authentication mode does not correct an incorrect country/region setting.

options.text: The regulatory country context can produce the wrong location/channel calculation for AFC.
options.feedback: The troubleshooting tip warns that the controller country code must match deployment country; a mismatch can lead to incorrect channel availability.

options.text: The DHCP lease file lacks the AP's MAC address.
options.feedback: NAC DHCP lease state is unrelated to AFC location and channel grants.

questions.stem: A FortiGate diagnostic shows lowi-pos-type=gps. What does this prove?

options.text: It proves that the AFC server returned every 6 GHz channel.
options.feedback: Position source and AFC authorization are separate stages.

options.text: It proves the AP is using Standard Power at maximum EIRP.
options.feedback: A GPS fix does not prove the granted power level or selected channel.

options.text: It proves the AP's country code is correct.
options.feedback: The coordinate source does not validate the controller's regulatory-domain configuration.

options.text: It proves the coordinate source is GPS, not that AFC granted a channel.
options.feedback: The WTP diagnostic exposes the position source; AFC status and response must be checked separately.

questions.stem: Which command pair most directly distinguishes an AFC request from its response?

options.text: Dump afc_request.txt and afc_response.txt with cw_diag.
options.feedback: The request and response dumps let the operator inspect what location information was sent and what channel availability was returned.

options.text: Use diagnose sys session list and diagnose firewall iprope list.
options.feedback: Those commands inspect firewall sessions/policy internals, not AFC exchanges.

options.text: Use get system status and diagnose hardware sysinfo memory.
options.feedback: System inventory and memory output do not show the AFC request/response.

options.text: Use diagnose switch-controller switch-info dhcp-snooping database.
options.feedback: That command is for managed-switch DHCP bindings.

questions.stem: A bridged AP is discovered, but downstream clients are not controlled by FortiNAC Access Point Management. What topology step is required?

options.text: Create a new FortiNAC RADIUS realm for every client MAC.
options.feedback: The documented AP-management mechanism uses the AP-facing switch port and DHCP leases, not per-client RADIUS realms.

options.text: Move the AP-facing upstream switch port into the Access Point Management group and remove the AP from Bridging Devices.
options.feedback: FortiNAC must associate the AP with the upstream switch interface and the correct group; AP discovery alone is not sufficient.

options.text: Mark the AP-facing interface as a user-defined uplink.
options.feedback: The guide instructs undoing the incorrect uplink designation so the AP is represented correctly.

options.text: Enable FortiGate IPAM unique allocation on the AP.
options.feedback: IPAM firewall-address allocation does not configure FortiNAC AP management.

questions.stem: A host behind an AP uses a static IP that is absent from FortiNAC's DHCP lease file. What should occur?

options.text: FortiNAC silently adds the static address to the DHCP lease file.
options.feedback: The guide describes event generation, not automatic trust of an untracked static address.

options.text: The AP is automatically removed from the switch inventory.
options.feedback: The event concerns the downstream host address, not AP inventory.

options.text: FortiNAC generates a StaticIPAddress event that can be mapped to an alarm/action.
options.feedback: The event is the documented response when the host MAC is not present in the FortiNAC-maintained DHCP lease file.

options.text: FortiNAC immediately moves every connected host to Isolation.
options.feedback: The feature's documented limitation says an already-connected production host may remain until lease expiry or disconnect.

questions.stem: How does FortiNAC distinguish authorized and unauthorized hosts in this AP-management design?

options.text: It changes the AP's radio channel based on host role.
options.feedback: Radio channel selection is unrelated to FortiNAC DHCP/DNS steering.

options.text: It tags the host with a pxGrid Session State.
options.feedback: pxGrid is a separate FortiManager/Cisco ISE integration.

options.text: It uses only the SSID name to determine registration state.
options.feedback: The documented check is based on DHCP lease-file membership and associated host identity.

options.text: It updates DHCP with authorized MAC/IP entries and directs the two host classes to different DNS paths.
options.feedback: Authorized hosts receive valid DNS; unauthorized hosts receive FortiNAC AP-management DNS for state-based redirection.

questions.stem: A host is manually rescanned and fails a scan while already on the production network. What limitation applies?

options.text: It can remain on production until its lease expires or it disconnects.
options.feedback: The guide explicitly states there is no mechanism to move an already-connected AP-management host to Isolation on that rescan/failure event.

options.text: It is immediately quarantined by changing the AP's VLAN.
options.feedback: That immediate isolation behavior is not provided by this feature.

options.text: It is moved to a new IPAM pool on the FortiGate.
options.feedback: IPAM address allocation is not the AP-management scan-failure behavior.

options.text: It is disconnected by the FortiNAC DHCP server at the next renewal regardless of lease.
options.feedback: The guide describes remaining on production until lease expiry or disconnect, not an unconditional immediate disconnect.

questions.stem: Global MFA is enabled on FortiNAC-F. What does that setting do?

options.text: It enables 802.1X MFA for every endpoint on every SSID.
options.feedback: This feature protects the administrator GUI, not all endpoint network authentication.

options.text: It enables administrator GUI MFA for all administrators.
options.feedback: The global SMS/email setting applies MFA across all administrator accounts, while individual settings are per-admin.

options.text: It forces every FortiGate in the Security Fabric to use FortiToken.
options.feedback: FortiNAC-F administrator MFA does not configure FortiGate administrator policy.

options.text: It disables individual administrator settings and deletes their contact data.
options.feedback: Global enforcement does not imply that individual contact values are erased.

questions.stem: An administrator has no personal country code, while global SMS MFA defines one. Which value is used?

options.text: The country code is inferred from the FortiNAC-F appliance timezone.
options.feedback: Timezone does not replace the documented country-code inheritance rule.

options.text: SMS is sent without a country code.
options.feedback: The global default exists to supply the missing country code.

options.text: The global default country code is inherited for that administrator.
options.feedback: FortiNAC-F uses the global default only when the administrator has not configured a personal country code.

options.text: The administrator is exempt from MFA.
options.feedback: A missing personal country code does not automatically exempt the administrator.

questions.stem: SMS MFA fails for all FortiNAC-F administrators, but email MFA works. What should be investigated?

options.text: The DHCP snooping trusted server list.
options.feedback: That list controls switch DHCP security, not FortiNAC-F SMS delivery.

options.text: The FortiAnalyzer Asset Identity Center index.
options.feedback: Asset identity correlation does not send administrator MFA codes.

options.text: The FortiPAM WebSSH SSH Filter.
options.feedback: WebSSH secret settings do not affect FortiNAC-F administrator SMS delivery.

options.text: The global SMS configuration and REST SMS Gateway delivery path.
options.feedback: The guide documents REST SMS Gateway delivery for cases without a configured mobile provider; a shared SMS failure points to the global gateway path.

questions.stem: Which CLI command is documented to reset FortiNAC-F administrator MFA settings?

options.text: execute admin-ui reset-mfa-settings
options.feedback: This is the documented recovery command for resetting individual and global MFA settings.

options.text: diagnose system health-check reset
options.feedback: That is not the documented administrator MFA reset command.

options.text: execute fortiguard update-now
options.feedback: FortiGuard update execution does not reset administrator MFA configuration.

options.text: diagnose switch-controller switch-info dhcp-snooping database
options.feedback: That command displays managed-switch DHCP bindings and is unrelated to administrator MFA.

questions.stem: Which two REST API resources were added for FortiAuthenticator external IdP self-service?

options.text: /radiusclients/ and /radsecaccounts/
options.feedback: Those names are not the documented external-IdP resource paths.

options.text: /remotesamlservers/ and /samlidpusersources/
options.feedback: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 adds separate resources for remote SAML servers and SAML IdP user sources.

options.text: /localusers/ and /fortitokens/
options.feedback: Local users are a separate endpoint; FortiToken resources are not the two new IdP resources.

options.text: /oauthclients/ and /samlcertificates/
options.feedback: Those paths are not the two resources identified in the release notes.

questions.stem: An automation engineer needs the exact methods and JSON fields for the new FAC resources. What is the authoritative discovery point?

options.text: A guessed POST body copied from a different FAC release.
options.feedback: Version-specific fields should be taken from the deployed API schema, not guessed.

options.text: The FortiGate firewall policy GUI.
options.feedback: A firewall policy GUI does not document FortiAuthenticator REST resource schemas.

options.text: The built-in Swagger UI at https://<FAC_IP>/api/v2/docs.
options.feedback: The release notes direct administrators to the embedded Swagger UI for the full REST API schema and endpoint operations.

options.text: The FortiNAC-F administrator MFA page.
options.feedback: That page documents another product's GUI authentication feature.

questions.stem: An API call creates a remote SAML server, but users still have no group mapping. What should be checked?

options.text: The FortiGate IPAM subnet allocation rule.
options.feedback: IPAM has no role in FAC SAML group sourcing.

options.text: The FortiSwitch DAI binding database.
options.feedback: Layer-2 ARP validation does not populate FAC identity groups.

options.text: The FortiPAM WebSSH secret's SSH Auto-Password option.
options.feedback: That setting is unrelated to FAC SAML user-source configuration.

options.text: The separate SAML IdP user-source resource and its mapping to the remote IdP.
options.feedback: The server and user-source are distinct resources; creating one does not prove the user-source mapping exists.

questions.stem: The API response confirms that both FAC resources exist. What remains necessary before claiming federation works?

options.text: Validate metadata/certificate trust and perform an end-to-end SAML assertion and group-mapping test.
options.feedback: Resource creation is only a configuration step; trust, assertion attributes, and user/group mapping must be proven by an actual SAML transaction.

options.text: Assume the IdP is healthy because the REST API returned success.
options.feedback: API resource creation does not validate the remote SAML exchange.

options.text: Disable certificate validation so the next login succeeds.
options.feedback: Disabling validation weakens trust and does not establish correct metadata or signing keys.

options.text: Wait for FortiGate IPAM to allocate a new subnet.
options.feedback: Network address allocation does not validate a SAML assertion.

questions.stem: A target SSH server prompts for an OTP after the user launches a FortiPAM WebSSH secret. Who validates that second factor?

options.text: FortiPAM validates the target's TOTP seed locally in every case.
options.feedback: The feature is designed to relay target-issued real-time codes; FortiPAM need not store the target TOTP seed.

options.text: The target SSH server validates the code after WebSSH relays the challenge and response.
options.feedback: The target emits the interactive challenge and remains authoritative for the target-side second-factor decision.

options.text: FortiGate IPAM validates the token against the VPN pool.
options.feedback: IPAM does not perform SSH second-factor authentication.

options.text: FortiAnalyzer validates the OTP from the Threat Posture Timeline.
options.feedback: FortiAnalyzer's AI timeline is not an SSH authentication service.

questions.stem: A user enters an incorrect WebSSH target OTP. What is the documented recovery behavior?

options.text: Keep entering codes until the SSH server accepts one.
options.feedback: The same connection does not support another attempt after an incorrect code.

options.text: Reset the FortiPAM global administrator MFA settings.
options.feedback: That reset affects administrator GUI MFA, not the target SSH challenge.

options.text: Close the session and relaunch the secret; the same connection cannot retry the challenge.
options.feedback: FortiPAM 1.9 documents that an incorrect token cannot be retried within the same SSH connection.

options.text: Force a FortiNAC-F HA failover to clear the prompt.
options.feedback: HA failover is unrelated to the WebSSH session's target-issued challenge.

questions.stem: FortiAuthenticator SMS/email challenge delivery is not relayed in WebSSH. Which secret-side setting can satisfy the documented prerequisite?

options.text: Enable DHCP snooping on the FortiPAM interface.
options.feedback: DHCP snooping is a switch feature and does not configure WebSSH.

options.text: Set the secret to a FortiGate IPAM address object.
options.feedback: IPAM address objects are not WebSSH secret prerequisites.

options.text: Change the FortiAnalyzer timeline timeframe.
options.feedback: A timeline timeframe does not affect SSH challenge handling.

options.text: Enable SSH service with a selected SSH Filter, even an empty filter profile.
options.feedback: The guide lists SSH service with a filter as one of the accepted SSH-related settings for SMS/email relay.

questions.stem: FortiToken Mobile push behaves inconsistently for a target's WebSSH challenge. What does FortiPAM recommend?

options.text: Use manual entry of the real-time token code for best reliability.
options.feedback: The 1.9 guide notes that automatic push can be inconsistent in some environments and recommends manual code entry.

options.text: Disable target-side MFA permanently.
options.feedback: The recommendation is a more reliable input method, not removing the target's security control.

options.text: Convert the target account to password-only authentication.
options.feedback: Password-only would bypass the challenge instead of solving the relay issue.

options.text: Change the FortiPAM API key expiration date.
options.feedback: API key lifecycle does not govern target-side WebSSH 2FA delivery.

questions.stem: What does the FortiSIEM triggeringEvents/start endpoint return for the asynchronous workflow?

options.text: The complete triggering-event payload in the same response.
options.feedback: The purpose of the new API is to return a job identifier rather than wait synchronously for the full payload.

options.text: A queryId that identifies the background retrieval job.
options.feedback: The start endpoint accepts incident/time parameters and returns a queryId used by progress and result endpoints.

options.text: A FortiGate IPAM allocation identifier.
options.feedback: The endpoint retrieves SIEM incident evidence, not network address allocations.

options.text: A FortiAnalyzer incident number that closes the incident.
options.feedback: The queryId is a job handle and does not close or change the incident.

questions.stem: When should the integration call the FortiSIEM triggeringEvents/result/{queryId} endpoint?

options.text: Immediately after receiving any HTTP 200 from start.
options.feedback: Start acceptance does not mean the asynchronous query has completed.

options.text: Before calling the start endpoint.
options.feedback: A result endpoint requires a queryId created by the start request.

options.text: After the progress endpoint reports 100 percent.
options.feedback: The documented sequence is start, poll progress, then retrieve results once progress reaches 100 percent.

options.text: Only after the incident has been closed.
options.feedback: Incident closure is not the completion condition documented for this API.

questions.stem: A SIEM integration receives the right queryId but the wrong events. Which inputs should be compared first?

options.text: The FortiGate country code and AP GPS position.
options.feedback: Wireless regulatory inputs do not scope a FortiSIEM incident query.

options.text: The FortiSwitch trusted DHCP server list.
options.feedback: Switch DHCP trust has no effect on the incident query parameters.

options.text: The FortiPAM WebSSH SSH Filter name.
options.feedback: Secret launcher settings do not determine SIEM query scope.

options.text: The incidentId, timeFrom, and timeTo used in the start request.
options.feedback: The API query is scoped by incident ID and time window; incorrect bounds produce a technically successful but semantically wrong result.

questions.stem: Why is the queryId workflow preferable for long triggering-event retrieval?

options.text: It separates job acceptance, progress monitoring, and result retrieval instead of holding one request open.
options.feedback: The asynchronous design avoids requiring the caller to wait for the full query response in a single synchronous request.

options.text: It automatically changes the incident severity while querying.
options.feedback: The API enhancement is about retrieval lifecycle, not incident severity mutation.

options.text: It guarantees the query returns every event in the SIEM database.
options.feedback: The query remains bounded by the requested incident and time range.

options.text: It removes the need for API authentication.
options.feedback: Asynchronous execution does not remove the API's authentication requirements.

questions.stem: A browser-only contractor device cannot run FortiClient but must send web traffic through an encrypted path to FortiSASE. Which steering method fits?

options.text: FortiClient agent tunnel with full tunneling.
options.feedback: The scenario explicitly cannot install FortiClient on the endpoint.

options.text: Private Proxy using a Branch On-ramp IPsec tunnel.
options.feedback: Private Proxy is designed for clients without FortiClient and carries proxy traffic from Branch On-ramp to FortiSASE over an encrypted tunnel.

options.text: FortiNAC Access Point Management.
options.feedback: That feature controls bridged AP clients using DHCP leases and DNS steering.

options.text: FortiManager pxGrid connector.
options.feedback: pxGrid imports Cisco ISE identity context and does not steer proxy traffic.

questions.stem: Private Proxy cannot be enabled on a new FortiSASE instance. What prerequisite is likely missing?

options.text: A FortiAnalyzer FortiAI license.
options.feedback: FortiAI licensing is unrelated to FortiSASE Private Proxy.

options.text: A FortiSwitch DHCP snooping static entry.
options.feedback: Switch bindings do not enable a FortiSASE traffic-steering feature.

options.text: Select-availability enablement, licensed Branch On-ramp, dedicated IP, and BGP configuration.
options.feedback: Private Proxy is not enabled by default and requires Branch On-ramp licensing/dedicated IP plus BGP before activation.

options.text: A FortiNAC-F global MFA country code.
options.feedback: Administrator OTP delivery is unrelated to Private Proxy prerequisites.

questions.stem: Deep inspection is enabled for Private Proxy users, but browsers report certificate errors. What is required?

options.text: Install the FortiManager pxGrid client certificate on every browser.
options.feedback: pxGrid certificates are for ISE connector trust, not the FortiSASE inspection CA.

options.text: Add a DHCP-snooping static binding for the browser MAC.
options.feedback: A DHCP binding does not establish TLS inspection trust.

options.text: Disable BGP on the Branch On-ramp device.
options.feedback: BGP is a prerequisite for Private Proxy; disabling it would make the path worse.

options.text: Install the FortiSASE CA certificate on the proxy-user endpoints.
options.feedback: The architecture guide requires the FortiSASE CA on endpoints when deep inspection is enabled so inspected TLS sessions are trusted.

questions.stem: FortiSASE cannot identify individual Private Proxy users by source IP. Which design condition is required for IP-based authentication?

options.text: Configure SSO and disable NAT on the On-ramp firewall policy.
options.feedback: The documented IP-based authentication mode requires SSO and source-IP preservation; NAT must be disabled so each client remains unique.

options.text: Enable NAT and share one translated source IP among clients.
options.feedback: Shared NAT addresses collapse multiple users and prevent per-client IP tracking.

options.text: Use only the FortiGate device serial number as the user identity.
options.feedback: Device serials do not replace the SSO/no-NAT requirement for IP-based authentication.

options.text: Change the proxy port from 8080 to 443.
options.feedback: A port change does not preserve client source identity.

questions.stem: Which statement about FortiSASE Private Proxy availability and compatibility is correct?

options.text: It is enabled by default for all new instances and has no dependencies.
options.feedback: The guide explicitly identifies it as select availability and lists Branch On-ramp/BGP prerequisites.

options.text: It is select availability and has migration/proxy-toggle compatibility caveats on existing instances.
options.feedback: The feature is not enabled by default, and the guide warns that existing instances using SSO Private Proxy are incompatible with certain proxy migration and disable/re-enable transitions.

options.text: It works only with FortiClient agent tunnels.
options.feedback: Private Proxy is intended for devices where FortiClient installation is not feasible.

options.text: It automatically provides private-resource access without SPA licensing.
options.feedback: Private-resource access requires optional SPA licensing and configuration.

questions.stem: FortiOS 8.0 packet-duplication thresholds are configured in what unit?

options.text: Milliseconds of latency per SLA probe.
options.feedback: Latency is a separate SD-WAN performance measurement, not the duplication bandwidth threshold unit.

options.text: Percent of monthly quota consumed.
options.feedback: Monthly quota steering is a different feature from packet-duplication bandwidth thresholds.

options.text: Kilobytes per second, with separate upstream, downstream, and bidirectional values.
options.feedback: The feature defines upbandwidth, dwbandwidth, and bibandwidth thresholds in KB/s.

options.text: Number of duplicated packets per second.
options.feedback: The values represent bandwidth thresholds, not a packet-count limit.

questions.stem: Two overlays share one physical underlay. Which measurement choice best detects congestion on that shared circuit?

options.text: Measure each overlay independently in every case.
options.feedback: Overlay measurement can hide shared physical congestion when multiple tunnels use the same underlay.

options.text: Use only the SLA latency score.
options.feedback: The duplication gate uses bandwidth measurement, not the SLA score.

options.text: Measure the FortiAnalyzer log-forwarding interface.
options.feedback: A logging interface is unrelated to the SD-WAN member's underlay utilization.

options.text: Set duplication-threshold-bandwidth to underlay.
options.feedback: Underlay measurement evaluates the shared physical path, so overlays mapped to that member respond to its aggregate utilization.

questions.stem: When the configured duplication threshold is exceeded, what should happen to the original traffic?

options.text: The additional duplicate copies stop; normal forwarding of the original traffic continues.
options.feedback: The feature gates packet duplication, not the original SD-WAN forwarding decision.

options.text: The original packet is dropped by the duplication engine.
options.feedback: The feature description says duplication stops; it does not say the original flow is dropped.

options.text: The member is removed from every SD-WAN service.
options.feedback: A duplication threshold is not the same as an SLA-driven member health decision.

options.text: The tunnel is automatically torn down.
options.feedback: The threshold controls duplicate copies and does not describe tunnel teardown.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a duplication threshold from monthly quota steering?

options.text: Both features are identical and use the same byte counter.
options.feedback: The documentation lists them as separate SD-WAN features with different control semantics.

options.text: A duplication threshold gates extra packet copies based on current member bandwidth; quota steering controls interface usage based on accumulated volume.
options.feedback: The two features have different inputs and actions: instantaneous directional utilization for duplication versus monthly traffic-volume policy.

options.text: Quota steering changes only packet DSCP while duplication thresholds change route priority.
options.feedback: Those are not the documented behaviors of either feature.

options.text: Duplication thresholds are evaluated only once per month.
options.feedback: The threshold is evaluated before duplication based on utilized bandwidth.

questions.stem: A FortiAnalyzer timeline chart is visible and a FortiSIEM queryId has been returned. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Both prove that every underlying event was fully collected.
options.feedback: Neither a chart nor a job identifier proves complete source telemetry by itself.

options.text: Both are simply static dashboards and require no further verification.
options.feedback: The SIEM query is asynchronous, and the timeline's source logs/time window must be examined.

options.text: The queryId is the FortiAnalyzer endpoint identity key.
options.feedback: The queryId belongs to the FortiSIEM triggering-events job, not Asset Identity Center.

questions.stem: A team enables FortiSwitch DAI and FortiGate IPAM unique allocation during the same change window. Which evidence should be validated independently?

options.text: Only the FortiGate Fabric connector status.
options.feedback: Fabric connectivity does not prove either the switch binding database or unique subnet allocation.

options.text: Only the DHCP client lease on one endpoint.
options.feedback: A client lease does not prove DAI/source guard enforcement or per-device IPAM uniqueness.

options.text: Only the FortiAnalyzer AI summary.
options.feedback: An AI summary cannot replace direct configuration and data-plane verification for either feature.
